text:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH — multiple websocket/SSE disconnects detected for customer celestis (vpc gateway). 5xx rate stable but streaming aborts spiking since 14:02 UTC. Alert rule: vpc.appgw.stream.disconnect.rate > 3/min
oncall-maya: ack — paging in.
oncall-maya: joining zoom, pulling logs now. any recent deploys to runtime or routing? @paul-runtime
paul-runtime: no deploys in last 3h from runtime. routing config for celestis hasn't changed since yesterday.
olivia-cust-eng: celestis-ops reporting user sessions dropped during long responses (30s+). They see client-side reconnects and some 499s at their ingress.
sam-support: customer impact: approx 120 unique sessions over last 20m, mainly on their mobile app via in-house app-gw. They call it "mid-stream reset" — screenshots with connection reset.
paul-runtime: grabbing trace for a sample session: websocket established -> 20s of tokens -> client side connection reset observed between app-gw and our VPC ingress, HTTP code 499 on their side.
paul-runtime: suspect proxy timeout or aggressive max_inflight on their gateway + our keepalive pattern.
olivia-cust-eng: they're using an nginx-based app‑gateway with default keepalive/read_timeout (60s). They do have some custom retry middleware.
oncall-maya: mitigation plan A: ask celestis to raise proxy_read_timeout and proxy_send_timeout to 180s temporarily and disable request-level retry middleware for streaming endpoints.
oncall-maya: mitigation plan B (if A not possible): enable server-side keepalive pings from our side and fallback to chunked non-streaming responses for this tenant for longer responses.
celestis-ops: can increase timeouts, but need exact config snippet and we want a hotfix from redwood for the keepalive before changing retries.
paul-runtime: sending nginx snippet for them to apply now:
```
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_read_timeout 180s;
proxy_send_timeout 180s;
proxy_http_version 1.1;
proxy_set_header Connection "";
```
sam-support: shared snippet with celestis-ops at 14:12 UTC, they're applying now.
raj-product: is this tenant-isolation safe? will changing our server behavior affect other customers in the VPC pool?
paul-runtime: yes — we can toggle tenant-level behavior via routing header (x-tenant-id) on the routing layer; enabling keepalive pings is per-tenant flag, safe for dedicated pool.
oncall-maya: applying tenant flag to enable keepalive pings for celestis now (ephemeral change) — rolling patch to edge: enabling WS ping every 25s and extended idle expiry to 200s for that tenant.
incident-bot: Action logged: oncall-maya enabled tenant:celestis ws-keepalive at 14:18 UTC.
paul-runtime: monitoring connections — saw immediate drop in disconnects for new sessions after 14:20 UTC. older sessions still bouncing while gateway re-applies config.
celestis-ops: confirmed proxy change applied at 14:22 UTC, reconnects reduced, app team reports smoother playback.
sam-support: customer impact estimate: peak client error rate down from 6% -> 0.8% over last 10m. still seeing rare 502s during reconnects.
paul-runtime: follow-up: we've queued a graceful-fallback patch for longer responses where streaming is not stable — switch to chunked transfer with content-length-less streaming and periodic flush to client. Will rollout to canary for celestis in 30m.
olivia-cust-eng: celestis requests a post-mortem and a runbook for future incidents — they need exact steps we took and suggested permanent gateway tuning.
oncall-maya: noted. I'll draft runbook and post in /incidents and tag celestis support.
raj-product: flagging for Dedicated / VPC docs update: include recommended app-gw nginx/haproxy settings for streaming + mobile SDK reconnection guidance.
celestis-ops: appreciate the quick help. we'll keep monitoring and will report if anything recurs.
oncall-maya: closing incident thread in slack when stable. monitoring window set to 60 minutes after last error.
incident-bot: Incident state -> mitigation applied. Monitoring for 1h. Incident closed (mitigated) at 14:34 UTC pending post-mortem.
